findings.finding: Opening book equity is stale: the residual-income case opens at common equity 11,290,948k dated 2025-12-31 (engine warning stale_balance_sheet, high), although the Q2 2026 IFRS statements in the pack give equity attributable to the parent 13,249,670k at 2026-06-30 (nm_equity_2026q2, dc_fs_q2_2026), +17.3%. The assumption's own falsifier (a later primary balance sheet more than 2% different) is triggered. Every scenario value and yearly path scales from this book: base FY2027 net income 3.32bn (EPS 0.684) is about flat on the tax-normalized 2026 run rate (H1 2026 NI 1,932.5m at an 11.8% tax rate, about 3.25bn a year at the FY2025 25.8% rate) and below the reported H1 run rate (3.87bn). Base 7.14 / bear 2.42 / bull 8.73 against a quote of 11.65 therefore understate the starting point. The table currently withholds a fair value, but value.json ran=true would let deliver freeze this base case in the ledger.
findings.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json val.case.opening.book_equity and fc.assumptions open_balance (statement_as_of 2025-12-31); fc.warnings stale_balance_sheet; evidence nm_equity_2026q2 / dc_fs_q2_2026
findings.fix: Repair: open the case at the 2026-06-30 parent equity 13,249,670k (dc_fs_q2_2026) with the H1 2026 profit and buyback rolled in (the engine reads only companyfacts, which has no 6-K quarters: supply it through the pack/inputs as a reported opening balance), and rerun ticker-value. If the engine cannot take a 6-K balance sheet, keep the result a draft, say the book is six months stale next to the result, and do not freeze the base case.

findings.finding: Book growth is pinned at the engine's generic BOOK_GROWTH_CAP of 8%/yr, and the payout rationale calls this 'its own five-year common-equity growth 8.0%'. That is false: Nu's own common equity grew 4,441m (2021) -> 11,291m (2025), about 26%/yr; 6,406m (2023) -> 11,291m (2025), about 33%/yr; and +17% in H1 2026 alone (to 13,250m), mostly retained earnings plus BRL translation, not issuance. The cap (forecast_financials.py BOOK_GROWTH_CAP) is a rule, not company data. Through payout = max(0.5, 1 - g/ROE) it forces base payouts of 73-77% (bull similar) for ten years, so base EPS grows only about 6-7%/yr (0.684 -> 0.830 by 2030) against reported NI growth of +46% in FY2025 and +62% y/y in H1 2026 (about +36% tax-normalized). Retained profit at a 26-29% ROE against an 11.2% cost of equity is the main value driver of a bank in residual income, so this rule largely sets the result. The binding company constraint is regulatory capital, not an 8% cap (see the CET1 finding).
findings.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json fc.assumptions payout (rationale) and fc.paths base/bull payout_fraction; val.case.scenarios[*].periods[*].payout_fraction; factbook equity I@2021..2025; nm_equity_2026q2
findings.fix: Repair/analyst: replace the capped book-growth path with a company-evidenced retention path: book growth from own history (2023-2025 and H1 2026), fading, and limited by the CET1 headroom (RWA growth vs CET1 capital, 1.85bn excess over the minimum) plus the 1.0bn buyback actually authorised. If the engine accepts no such override, show '8% book growth is an engine cap, not Nu's data' next to the result as a visible gap and keep it a draft. The rationale text must stop calling 8% the company's own growth.

findings.finding: Payout is the 50% default with warning payout_unknown 'no dividend or buyback history', but the pack documents buybacks: 40.66m Class A shares for US$500.4m in Q2 2026 under a US$1.0bn program (499.6m left to June 2027), and no dividend (nm_buybacks_2026h1, dc_k_buyback). Actual capital return is about 26% of H1 2026 profit (500.4 / 1,932.5) or about 1bn a year (about 25-30% of normalized profit), against the 50% floor and the 73-77% the base path actually uses.
findings.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json fc.anchors.payout 0.5, fc.warnings payout_unknown, fc.assumptions payout; evidence nm_buybacks_2026h1, dc_k_buyback
findings.fix: Supply the evidenced distribution history (H1 2026 buyback 500.4m, no dividend; the 1.0bn authorisation) so the payout anchor is about 25-30%, bounded by CET1; otherwise state next to the result that the payout is a model default contradicted by the filing.

findings.finding: Regulatory capital is not checked (risk_weighted_assets 0, required_capital_ratio 0 in every period; warning regulatory_capital_not_checked), although the pack has the numbers: Brazilian prudential conglomerate CET1 13.0% -> 11.9% (Dec 2025 -> Jun 2026), RWA 31.1bn -> 35.7bn (+14.7% in six months), CET1 capital 4.05bn -> 4.26bn, minimum 10.5%, excess about 1.85bn (understand/business.json, dc_fs_q2_2026). The key risk cites this falling CET1, yet the model cannot show whether any payout or growth path is permitted. Note the CET1 capital (4.26bn) sits in the regulated Brazilian entities, far below the 13.25bn holding-company equity.
findings.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json val.case.scenarios[*].periods[*].risk_weighted_assets / required_capital_ratio; assumption regulatory_capital; understand/business.json capital item; position/core.json key_risk
findings.fix: Feed RWA (35.7bn at 2026-06-30) and the required CET1 ratio with buffers (10.5%) from dc_fs_q2_2026 into the regulatory_capital assumption so the engine checks the payout; or state next to the result that the growth and payout paths are unchecked against CET1.

findings.finding: No country risk premium: cost of equity 11.18% = US risk-free 4.98% + ERP 4.20% + 1.5% growth stage + 0.5% balance sheet, with no Brazil premium. The table says country risk was not computed because 'no readable revenue split by country'. The pack does hold one (Brazil 91.3% / Mexico 6.7% of interest-and-fee revenue FY2025; Brazil 91.1% in Q2 2026), but under a metric whose scope review_trace flagged as narrower than total revenue. A Brazil-centred bank valued in USD at a US-only rate makes the value too high, the opposite direction to the two critical findings. It must be fixed together with them.
findings.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json fc.cost_of_equity.components; out/table_he.md last bullet; gather/macro.json mc_f_rev_br / mc_f_rev_mx / mc_f_rev_ot
findings.fix: Relabel the regional facts with their basis (interest-and-fee revenue, excludes financial-instrument gains) in the form the --country-risk step reads, so the engine computes the exposure-weighted CRP; rerun ticker-value. If it still cannot, show the missing Brazil premium next to the result.

findings.finding: The analyst's ROE views were not applied to the engine case. value.json reports 3 overrides, but fc.overrides is empty with warning overrides_not_applied (the residual-income model takes no operating overrides). The engine base runs ROE 29.2% -> 28.1% (year 5) -> 19.6% terminal; the analyst's company_path base uses 26% (tax-normalized H1 2026 about 29%, less the CSLL rise to 17.5%/20% and capital needs). company_path flags capital_intensity_gap (high) in all three scenarios (bear 17% vs 10.2%, base 26% vs 19.6%, bull 32% vs 24.3%). So the fair value and the yearly table rest on different economics.
findings.where: value.json overrides; companies/NU/out/casefile.json fc.overrides, fc.warnings overrides_not_applied, company_path.flags capital_intensity_gap; position/path.json
findings.fix: Express the analyst's ROE and payout views as the RI case's evidenced ROE/payout paths (through the engine's financials options if available), so the engine and company_path share one ROE and retention. Otherwise state both numbers and the gap next to the result.

findings.finding: company_path multiples for years 4 and 5 are artefacts. The interim report date 2031-11-01 splits fiscal 2031 into a 10-month part (EPS 0.736) and a 2-month stub (EPS 0.151), and each is used as a full 'next fiscal year EPS'. So the base multiple jumps to 13.5x (year 4) and 67.9x (year 5): bear 13.3x/68.6x, bull 15.6x/78.6x. The values themselves (base 10.29 at year 5) come from the dividend sum and are not affected, but any multiple row shown for years 4-5 is meaningless.
findings.fix: Do not show company_path multiples for years 4-5 (or annualize the next-twelve-months EPS across the stub). Engine issue: report it to the owner; the repair pass cannot fix it in inputs.

findings.finding: The engine's 'trailing twelve months' ROE (30.30%) is FY2025 itself (by_year 2025-12-31 = 0.30299 = ttm), because companyfacts has no 6-K quarters. So the abnormal 14.2% Q2 2026 tax rate (H1 11.8%, deferred tax benefit -991m) is not in the engine's ROE. The engine's starting ROE 29.2% is close to the analyst's tax-normalized H1 2026 figure of about 29%. That is acceptable, but the label is wrong and the ROE history stops at 2025-12-31. The pre_breakeven_roe_excluded change works as described: median 28.1% and lower quartile 18.2% over 2023-2025 only (short_roe_history, high: three profitable years span no credit cycle, while NPL 90+ is at 6.9%).
findings.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json fc.anchors.roe (ttm, history), fc.assumptions roe_history rationale; fc.warnings pre_breakeven_roe_excluded, short_roe_history
findings.fix: Label the 'trailing' ROE as FY2025. When the opening book moves to 2026-06-30, use a tax-normalized H1 2026 ROE (about 29% at a 25.8% rate), never the reported 14.2%-tax quarter. Keep short_roe_history visible next to the bear case.

findings.finding: Share count 4,855,673,632 is the 20-F cover count dated 2025-12-31. The pack has 4,860.6m on 2026-03-01 (3,838.0m Class A + 1,022.6m Class B), less 40.66m Class A repurchased in Q2 2026 (treasury); the Q2 2026 diluted weighted average is 4,904.8m (RSU dilution about 1%). This is within the 1% falsifier, but it is neither point-in-time at as_of nor diluted, and it is held constant while buybacks are treated as dividends.
findings.where: companies/NU/out/casefile.json val.case.opening.shares, fc.assumptions shares_point; evidence identity / nm_buybacks_2026h1 / nm_ shares_diluted_wavg Q2 2026
findings.fix: Use the 2026-06-30 point-in-time count (2026-03-01 count less the 40.66m repurchased, plus vested RSUs) and add the dilutive RSUs/options for per-share value.

findings.finding: Bear thesis says 'then no excess return', but its terminal ROE is 10.18%, one point below the 11.18% cost of equity, at 4.98% perpetual growth. That is perpetual value destruction (terminal P/B 0.84), not zero excess return.
findings.fix: Either state the bear as 'ROE below the cost of equity for good' with evidence, or set terminal ROE = cost of equity (P/B 1.0).

findings.finding: The quote 11.65 is an after-hours IB print (2026-10-30 23:56 UTC, is_close false). The official 2026-10-30 close is 11.61 (review_trace), a 0.3% difference.
findings.fix: Use the 11.61 close (or a fresh snapshot) on the rerun.
